question.value: Can 3D SPH dust+gas simulations of PDS 70 with two migrating, accreting embedded planets reach a stable resonant configuration and reproduce the observed ALMA mm continuum, 12CO and SPHERE scattered-light features?

We model both dust and gas, aiming to understand the physical origin of features observed in mm and scattered light images.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA 2013.1.00592.S.

analysis_steps.goal: Run 3D dust+gas SPH simulations of two embedded migrating planets

method.value: PHANTOM SPH with one-fluid dust, 1 mm grains, planets and star as sink particles that accrete and migrate, three runs with different initial planet masses and positions

evidence.quote: We perform a set of three dust and gas hydrodynamics simulations in 3D using PHANTOM, a smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) code (cite: Price2018).
The planets and the central star are included in the code as sink particles, characterized by an initial mass, position and sink radius.

key_parameters.value: 10^6 SPH particles; M_star = 0.8 Msun; R_out = 120 au; R_in = 5 au (Sim 1) or 2 au (Sim 2, 3); R_0 = 100 au; Sigma_0 = 1.07 g cm^-2; H/R = 0.05 at R_0; alpha_SS = 0.005; dust 1 mm, dust-to-gas 0.01

evidence.quote: representing the disc with $10^6$ SPH particles
The outer radius is fixed in all the simulations, $R_{\rm out}=120$ au.
in order to have a value for the effective (cite: SS1973) viscosity of $\alpha_{\rm SS}=0.005$

key_parameters.value: Initial planet masses and positions, and sink radii as fractions of the Hill radius, listed per simulation in Table 1

evidence.quote: Initial conditions for the three simulations, called sim 1, sim 2, sim 3.
We assume a locally isothermal equation of state with a sound speed profile

assumptions.value: Dust initially coupled to gas (Stokes number below unity), justifying the one-fluid mode

evidence.quote: This implies that dust and the gas are initially coupled in the disc.

validation.value: Dependence of results on the sink radius was checked by varying it between simulations

evidence.quote: The value of the sink radius may affect the planetary accretion rate and thus their final mass, so we decided to check the dependence of our results on this parameter.

analysis_steps.goal: Radiative transfer of the snapshots into synthetic continuum and scattered-light images

method.value: MCFOST Monte Carlo radiative transfer on the SPH snapshot at t = 500 Torb, ray-traced images at 855 um, 2.11 and 2.25 um, then convolution with the observed ALMA beam

evidence.quote: we post-processed our simulation using the Monte Carlo radiative transfer code MCFOST (cite: Pinte2006; Pinte2009).
We then compute the source function by ray-tracing to produce the output images at the desired wavelengths.

claims.hypothesis: Planets that start lighter and farther out, free to migrate and accrete, can reach the observed mass, position and resonance of PDS 70 b and c
claims.experiment: Three 3D SPH runs with different initial planet masses and positions
claims.result: Planets lock into resonance; Sim 3 gives Planet b at ~18-20 au and Planet c at ~35-40 au
claims.finding: Planet migration and resonant locking produce a configuration compatible with observations

evidence.quote: We found that the two planets quickly lock into resonance with a ratio that is compatible with observational results as well as with previous 2D numerical simulations (cite: Bae2019).

claims.hypothesis: Observed mm and scattered-light features are explained by the accretion stream onto planet c without a circumplanetary disc
claims.experiment: MCFOST synthetic 855 um and ADI-processed 2.11/2.25 um images compared with ALMA and SPHERE data, plus a +180 deg control snapshot
claims.result: The mm spur and most intra-cavity IR features are reproduced; the dusty feature near planet b is absent
claims.finding: Planet-disc interactions alone explain most features, though the spur origin (CPD vs wake) stays unclear

evidence.quote: We show that features observed at infrared (scattered light) and millimetre (thermal continuum) wavelengths are naturally explained by the accretion stream onto the outer planet, without requiring a circumplanetary disc around planet c.
In all our images the dusty feature observed around the inner planet (Planet b) in (cite: Isella2019) is absent.

claims.hypothesis: The simulated 12CO emission matches the observed cavity and flux
claims.experiment: Synthetic 12CO J=3-2 moment 0 maps and azimuthal profiles versus Keppler2019
claims.result: Flux compatible, but the compact inner ring is not reproduced and the ring peak lies at 0.3 arcsec instead of 0.4
claims.finding: Models have too much gas in the cavity

evidence.loc: CO maps and mass accretion rate
evidence.quote: The flux value is compatible with the observed values.
however we fail to reproduce the compact inner ring found in the observations

claims.hypothesis: Simulated planetary accretion rates match the observed values
claims.experiment: Sink accretion rates versus time for each simulation
claims.result: Planet b rate consistent with observed; planet c rate strongly overestimated; outer planet accretes faster than the inner one
claims.finding: Absolute accretion rates cannot be constrained, only the relative ordering

evidence.loc: CO maps and mass accretion rate
evidence.quote: we appear to strongly overestimate the accretion rate onto Planet c
Our simulations did not allow us to firmly constrain the planetary accretion rates.

claims.hypothesis: Whether a dust ring forms between the two planets
claims.experiment: Tracking dust between the orbits in the three runs
claims.result: An inter-planetary ring forms in the first ~100 orbits but is accreted within ~100-150 orbits later
claims.finding: No long-lived dust ring between the planets, consistent with the observations

evidence.quote: the dust is not trapped between the orbits of the planets, but it is accreted onto the sinks

referee_caveats_inferred: Only three simulations with one disc setup, one grain size (1 mm) and a locally isothermal gas; resonance and ring positions may depend on these choices
The ALMA data are only used as published images; no quantitative fit statistic between models and data is given
Agreement is judged qualitatively by eye for the continuum and scattered-light features

reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The ALMA data are not reduced in this paper, and the results are largely qualitative image comparisons from long hydrodynamic runs.
